title: Read-only viewers can still drag and move people; sensors=undefined activates dnd-kit default sensors
detail: When isEditor is false, Board passes sensors={undefined} to DndContext intending to disable dragging. But dnd-kit's DndContext prop default is `sensors = defaultSensors` where defaultSensors = [PointerSensor (no activation constraint), KeyboardSensor] (verified in node_modules/@dnd-kit/core/dist/core.cjs.development.js lines 2465-2469 and 2860). So for viewers, drag is fully active. handleDragStart's `if (!isEditor) return;` only skips setting activeId/announce — it does not cancel the drag session — and handleDragEnd (lines 112-132) has NO isEditor check, so it calls movePerson() on drop. The draggable card still translates with the pointer (useDraggable transform applied in PersonCard), so a viewer in 唯讀模式 can visibly pick up a person, drop them, mutate board state, write to localStorage via the debounced save, log an audit entry, and trigger a Supabase upsert. Second concrete failure: because the default PointerSensor has no activation constraint, AbstractPointerSensor.handleStart() runs immediately on pointerdown and installs a capture-phase document click listener calling stopPropagation (core.cjs.development.js:1508-1513), so React's onClick on PersonCard never fires for viewers — clicking a card to open the HistoryDrawer is silently broken in read-only mode.
evidence:
<DndContext
  sensors={isEditor ? sensors : undefined}
  collisionDetection={closestCenter}
  ...
// handleDragEnd has no isEditor guard:
const person = peopleMap.get(personId);
if (person && person.area !== targetArea) {
  movePerson(personId, targetArea);
// dnd-kit source: sensors = defaultSensors, // [PointerSensor, KeyboardSensor]
suggestedFix: Pass an empty array instead of undefined (sensors={isEditor ? sensors : []}) — useSensors/DndContext accept it and no sensor will ever activate — and additionally guard handleDragEnd with `if (!isEditor) return;` as defense in depth.

(2) handleDragStart's `if (!isEditor) return` only skips setActiveId/announce — onDragStart cannot cancel a dnd-kit drag session. handleDragEnd (Board.tsx:112-132) has no isEditor guard and calls movePerson. (3) useBoard.movePerson (src/hooks/useBoard.ts:135-170) has no role guard: it writes an audit entry via logAuditEntry, mutates state (triggering the debounced saveBoard→localStorage), and fires the Supabase upsert via persistMove. title: Keyboard drag-and-drop is dead: explicit onKeyDown prop overwrites dnd-kit KeyboardSensor activator
detail: useDraggable's `listeners` object contains the merged sensor activators: onMouseDown (MouseSensor), onTouchStart (TouchSensor), and onKeyDown (KeyboardSensor). In the JSX, `{...listeners}` is spread first (line 131) and then `onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}` is written afterwards (line 138). Later JSX props override earlier spreads, so the KeyboardSensor's onKeyDown activator is completely replaced. Pressing Enter/Space on a focused card opens the HistoryDrawer (handleKeyDown calls onClick) and never starts a keyboard drag. The sr-only instructions Board renders ("Press Space or Enter to pick up a draggable item...", Board.tsx:382-384, referenced via aria-describedby="dnd-instructions") are therefore false — keyboard users cannot move anyone, on a board that includes KeyboardSensor in useSensors specifically for accessibility.
suggestedFix: Compose instead of override: call dnd-kit's handler first, e.g. onKeyDown={(e) => { listeners?.onKeyDown?.(e); if (!e.defaultPrevented) handleKeyDown(e); }} — or place the spread after the explicit prop and trigger the drawer via a different key/affordance so Enter/Space remain the pick-up keys.

verdicts.reasoning: Read PersonCard.tsx in full and Board.tsx in full, plus the installed @dnd-kit/core 6.3.1 dist source. Confirmed: (1) PersonCard.tsx:131-138 spreads {...listeners} then writes onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}, and JSX later-prop-wins semantics (unchanged in React 19) replaces the spread's onKeyDown; (2) @dnd-kit/core 6.3.1 defines KeyboardSensor.activators = [{eventName: 'onKeyDown', ...}] (core.esm.js:1343) merged into useDraggable's listeners via useCombineActivators, so the overwritten handler is exactly the keyboard drag activator; (3) handleKeyDown (lines 116-121) never delegates to listeners.onKeyDown — it only calls onClick on Enter/Space, so keyboard drag can never activate and Enter/Space opens the HistoryDrawer instead (onClick → handlePersonClick → setHistoryPerson, Board.tsx:140-142/287/387); (4) not intentional: Board.tsx:73 explicitly registers KeyboardSensor, Board.tsx:382-384 renders the sr-only keyboard drag instructions referenced by aria-describedby, and handleKeyDown's !e.defaultPrevented guard only makes sense if the sensor activator was expected to run first — the prop order defeats that design. No alternate handler path exists (attributes contains only aria props; the card div is the sole listeners target). Refutation attempts all failed; the bug is genuine.
verdicts.correctedDetail: Report is accurate. Minor scoping notes: impact is limited to keyboard-using editors (MouseSensor/TouchSensor activators onMouseDown/onTouchStart are not overridden, so mouse/touch drag still works, and read-only wall-display mode is unaffected); the adjacent onClick={onClick} after the spread is harmless since listeners contains no onClick. Fix is to chain: call listeners?.onKeyDown?.(e) before the click fallback, or place handleKeyDown logic so the sensor activator runs first (the existing !e.defaultPrevented guard already anticipates that ordering).

title: closestCenter makes drag-cancel impossible: releasing anywhere always assigns the person to the nearest area
detail: collisionDetection={closestCenter} computes the distance from the dragged card's center to EVERY registered droppable and returns all of them sorted ascending — it never requires intersection (verified in node_modules/@dnd-kit/core/dist/core.cjs.development.js:332-357: it pushes a collision for every droppableContainer that has a rect). With ~70 droppable areas registered, `over` is never null on drop. Consequences: (1) the `if (!over) { announce("Drag cancelled"); return; }` branch in handleDragEnd (lines 116-119) is dead code for pointer drags; (2) a user who picks up a card and tries to abort by releasing over the header, toolbar, or any blank gap silently moves the person to whichever area's center happens to be nearest (e.g., the Leader box at the top of the screen) — an unintended staffing change on a hospital board. Escape is the only way to abort, which a wall-display touch user does not have.
suggestedFix: Use pointerWithin (falling back to rectIntersection) for this distinct-dropzone layout: e.g. a custom collision detection `(args) => { const p = pointerWithin(args); return p.length ? p : rectIntersection(args); }` so drops outside any zone yield over=null and genuinely cancel.

verdicts.reasoning: Read Board.tsx in full around the citation (lines 1-350): collisionDetection={closestCenter} at line 270 on the single DndContext; handleDragEnd (112-132) has only the `if (!over)` cancel branch with no other validation. Verified installed @dnd-kit/core 6.3.1 source (dist/core.cjs.development.js): closestCenter pushes a collision for every droppableContainer that has a rect and sorts ascending — no intersection required — so `over` is the nearest of the always-mounted ~68 droppables (67 ALL_AREAS in board-constants.ts + unassigned pool) on every pointer/touch drop, making the !over branch effectively dead and drop-anywhere assign to the nearest area's center. Grep across src confirms no guards: AreaBox.tsx is the only useDroppable caller (no disabled), no pointerWithin/rectIntersection/custom detector, no over.data validation or distance threshold in handleDragEnd. Not intentional design: the author's own "Drag cancelled" drop-outside branch shows drop-to-cancel was expected. Mouse/Touch sensors are active for editors, and the Leader AreaBox sits in the header row, so the reported unintended-reassignment scenario on a touch wall display is genuine. Only nitpick: title says cancel is "impossible" but Escape (onDragCancel) still works — the report itself concedes this.

Verified all three legs of the claim against current code. (1) Board.tsx:270 uses collisionDetection={closestCenter}; handleDragEnd (lines 112-132) calls movePerson whenever `over` is non-null and the area differs, with no containment check, and the `if (!over)` branch at 116-119 is dead for pointer/touch drags since Escape routes through onDragCancel instead. (2) The installed @dnd-kit/core's closestCenter (node_modules/@dnd-kit/core/dist/core.cjs.development.js) pushes a collision for every droppable that has a rect — no intersection test — so `over` is never null on drop while any droppable is mounted. (3) Counted 68 always-mounted droppables (ALL_AREAS = 67 areas in board-constants.ts plus the 未分派 UnassignedPool), matching the reviewer's ~70. Reachable path: an editor on the touch wall display long-presses a card (TouchSensor 300ms), aborts by releasing over the header/toolbar/blank gap, and closestCenter assigns the person to the nearest area center — the Leader box literally sits in the header (Board.tsx:285). useBoard.movePerson then persists the move optimistically to localStorage, writes to Supabase assignments, and logs an audit entry, so it is a real persisted staffing change. Touch users have no Escape, so no abort exists. One nuance: AreaBox highlights via isOver, so the nearest target does light up during the drag — the move is not fully silent, but a user aborting quickly will not notice. Severity medium is an honest grade: editor-only, reversible, audit-logged, visually cued, but it is an unintended staffing change on a hospital board with no cancel affordance for touch. Standard fix: pointerWithin/rectIntersection composed with closestCenter fallback.
verdicts.correctedDetail: Claim is accurate as written, with two refinements: the droppable count is 68 (67 ALL_AREAS + the 未分派 unassigned pool), and the move is not entirely silent — closestCenter drives AreaBox's isOver highlight, so the nearest area lights up during the drag even when the pointer is over the header. The core defect stands: `over` is never null on pointer/touch drop, the !over cancel branch is dead code for those sensors, and releasing over non-droppable chrome reassigns the person to the nearest area (often Leader, which sits in the header), persisted to Supabase and audit-logged.

title: Importing while a playback is running corrupts playback state: stale steps fire and a second animated import never plays its first steps
detail: handleImport never stops an in-flight playback, and the render-phase auto-start guard only triggers when prevStepsLen.current === 0. Scenario A (animated import during an active playback): setPlaybackSteps(newSteps) runs while prevStepsLen.current is still the old non-zero length, so play() is never called for the new steps; meanwhile the running setTimeout chain in useDemoPlayback already captured the OLD step object (scheduleStep reads `const step = currentSteps[index]` at scheduling time) and fires movePerson for a person id that no longer exists in the replaced roster, then continues via stepsRef.current into the NEW steps array from the OLD index — so people 0..index-1 of the new import remain unassigned forever and progress/total are inconsistent. Scenario B (non-animated import during playback): playbackSteps is left untouched, so the old chain keeps firing moves for stale person ids against the replaced roster (no-op state updates, but persistMove still issues Supabase upserts with stale person_ids), and the PlaybackBar keeps showing stale names. The toolbar's 匯入班表 button remains fully accessible while PlaybackBar is shown, so this needs no unusual steps to hit. The queueMicrotask(() => playback.play()) side effect executed during render (line 190) is itself a render-phase side effect that this fragile ref-guard exists to protect.
suggestedFix: In handleImport, first call playback.stop() and setPlaybackSteps([]) before loading new people; move auto-start into a useEffect keyed on playbackSteps (e.g. useEffect(() => { if (playbackSteps.length > 0) playback.play(); }, [playbackSteps])) instead of a render-phase ref check, and have useDemoPlayback clear its pending timeout when the steps array identity changes.

All other mechanics confirmed: handleImport (Board.tsx:152-165) never calls playback.stop(); the render-phase auto-start guard (Board.tsx:187-194) only calls play() on a 0→non-zero transition of playbackSteps.length, and a replacing setPlaybackSteps never passes through empty, so a second animated import during playback never auto-plays; the 匯入班表 button stays enabled alongside PlaybackBar; movePerson (useBoard.ts:135-170) calls persistMove unconditionally even when the person id is absent from the roster; imported ids are fresh crypto.randomUUID() values so old step ids are always stale.

Attempted refutations all failed: there is no guard elsewhere preventing import during playback, no effect that stops or restarts the timeout chain when steps are replaced, and React 19 render semantics do not change the behavior — stepsRef.current is updated during the re-render that completes well before the 400-800ms step timeouts fire. Both scenarios occur as described: animated re-import never plays its first steps and fires one stale step into the new roster with inconsistent progress/total; non-animated import leaves the old chain firing stale moves and stale PlaybackBar names, issuing Supabase upserts with stale person_ids when configured.

title: Dragged card moves twice: original card applies translate transform while DragOverlay copy is also rendered
detail: DraggablePersonCard applies dnd-kit's transform to the in-place node (`translate(${transform.x}px, ${transform.y}px)`), but Board.tsx also renders a <DragOverlay>{activePerson ? <PersonCard overlay/> : null}</DragOverlay> (Board.tsx:380). With dnd-kit, when a DragOverlay is used the original draggable must NOT apply the transform (it should stay in place as a placeholder — which is clearly the intent here given the `isDragging ? "opacity-30 scale-95"` ghost styling). As written, every editor drag shows TWO cards following the cursor: the full-opacity DragOverlay copy plus the 30%-opacity original translating in lockstep underneath, and the source slot appears empty instead of showing a ghost placeholder. Visually confusing on the wall display and makes the drop origin ambiguous.
suggestedFix: Stop translating the original when an overlay is used: const style = isDragging ? { touchAction: "none" } : { touchAction: "pan-y" }; (drop the translate entirely) so the opacity-30 ghost stays in its slot and only the DragOverlay follows the cursor.

verdicts.correctedDetail: The core claim is correct: PersonCard.tsx:103-105 applies dnd-kit's transform to the in-place draggable while Board.tsx:380 also renders a DragOverlay copy, and @dnd-kit/core 6.3.1 (dist core.cjs.development.js:3407) does NOT nullify the original's transform when an overlay is used — so the original does translate with the cursor and the source slot loses its intended opacity-30/scale-95 in-place ghost. However, the claimed symptom of "TWO cards visibly following the cursor" is overstated: the overlay starts at the original's initial rect, moves with the same x/y delta, sits at zIndex 999, and is scale-105 vs the original's scale-95, so the 30%-opacity original is almost entirely occluded beneath it; it is also clipped by the overflow-y-auto/overflow-hidden source containers (Board.tsx:278/281/344/357) once dragged out of them. Actual user-visible defects: empty source slot instead of an in-place ghost (ambiguous drop origin), possible scrollable-overflow expansion/scrollbar flicker in the source container during drag, and visible double-image divergence only if the source container scrolls mid-drag (overlay transform excludes scroll delta, dist line 2993).

title: Fit-to-screen zoom is a no-op: it measures scrollWidth/scrollHeight of the very element that clips all overflow, so zoomLevel is always 1
detail: The recalc reads boardRef.current.scrollWidth/scrollHeight, but boardRef is the root div with `h-dvh overflow-hidden`, whose only child is the wrapper div that itself has `overflow-hidden` (line 281) and contains all content; every inner panel scrolls internally (overflow-y-auto). Because the wrapper clips its own overflow (and its flex min-size resolves to 0 since it is not overflow:visible), the root's scrollWidth/scrollHeight can never exceed its clientWidth/clientHeight, which equal the viewport. Therefore Math.min(vw/scrollWidth, vh/scrollHeight, 1) always evaluates to 1, setZoomLevel(1) is a no-op, and the 🔍 Fit button toggles its highlight without ever changing the layout — the wall-display feature it was built for is dead. Additionally, the useDebouncedCallback unmount cleanup (use-debounce.ts lines 16-22) clears the pending timer WITHOUT invoking the callback, so any pending save is also dropped whenever the Board unmounts (e.g. auth state change swaps AuthGuard to the login prompt, unmounting Board mid-debounce). Since localStorage is the app's actual source of truth on load (Supabase is never read), this is direct data loss.
suggestedFix: Add a flush mechanism: expose a flush() from useDebouncedCallback that runs the pending callback immediately; call it from a pagehide/beforeunload listener and from the unmount cleanup (flush instead of discard). localStorage.setItem is synchronous and safe in pagehide.

title: Realtime handler never fetches remote state — other clients' changes never appear, yet SyncIndicator turns green claiming "Synced"
detail: The postgres_changes subscription on `assignments` only executes `setLastSyncedAt(new Date())` — it neither uses the change payload nor re-fetches. A grep confirms no SELECT of assignments/people exists anywhere in src; board state is loaded exclusively from localStorage (initial-load effect, line 72). For the product's core purpose — multiple wall displays showing the same board — this means a change made on the editor's machine never reaches the wall display's board state. Worse, the wall display's SyncIndicator (SyncIndicator.tsx lines 35-39) flips to a green dot with "Synced Xs ago" precisely when a remote change arrives, asserting freshness while displaying stale assignments. The hospital staff looking at the wall see outdated room assignments labeled as just-synced.
suggestedFix: In the handler, apply the change payload to local state (payload.new contains person_id/area_id) or re-fetch the day's assignments and merge into `people`; only update lastSyncedAt after state is actually reconciled.

title: Audit log inserts always fail (names/local ids into UUID columns) and the error is fully swallowed — DB audit trail is permanently empty
detail: audit_log columns are UUIDs with FK constraints: `person_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES people(id)`, `from_area_id/to_area_id UUID REFERENCES areas(id)` (001_initial_schema.sql lines 41-43). logAuditEntry inserts `person_id: entry.personId` (local ids like "demo-1" or client UUIDs absent from the DB) and `from_area_id/to_area_id` as area NAME strings ("R1", "Leader") — every insert fails with a uuid/FK error. The `.then(() => {})` discards the PostgREST result object, ignoring its `error` field, so the failure is invisible: no console output, no UI state. Result: the audit history feature (a compliance feature for an OR) silently records nothing in the DB and survives only in a volatile in-memory array that is wiped on every page reload. useAuditLog's DB query also fails for the same id-format reason and silently falls back to the in-memory log (useAuditLog.ts lines 46-48), masking the breakage.
evidence:
(supabase.from("audit_log") as any)
  .insert({
    person_id: entry.personId,
    from_area_id: entry.fromArea,
    to_area_id: entry.toArea,
    action_type: entry.actionType,
    user_id: entry.userId ?? null,
  })
  .then(() => {}); // fire-and-forget
suggestedFix: Resolve area names to area UUIDs and ensure person ids match DB rows (see related findings), and at minimum inspect the result: `.then(({ error }) => { if (error) console.error("audit insert failed", error); })` so failures are detectable.

title: useAuditLog fetch has no cancellation — switching person while a request is in flight lets the stale response overwrite the new person's entries
detail: fetchEntries is recreated when personId changes and the effect re-runs, but the previous in-flight Supabase query is not cancelled and its .then callback has no staleness guard. Sequence: open HistoryDrawer for person A (request A starts, slow), click person B (request B starts, fast, setEntries(B-entries)), request A resolves last and calls setEntries with A's merged entries — the drawer now shows person A's history under person B's name. There is also no unmount guard, so the callback fires setState after the drawer closes. The merge path makes it worse because the fallback `getAuditLogForPerson(personId)` inside the callback closes over the OLD personId.
suggestedFix: Use the standard stale-flag pattern: in the effect, `let stale = false; ... if (!stale) setEntries(...); return () => { stale = true; };` (move the fetch body into the effect or pass an isStale getter into fetchEntries).

title: Playback auto-start is a render-phase side effect and never restarts when importing during an active playback
detail: The auto-start block mutates a ref and calls queueMicrotask(playback.play) during render (a React render-purity violation), and its guard `prevStepsLen.current === 0` makes a second animated import broken while a playback is still running: handleImport replaces playbackSteps with the new array, but since prevStepsLen.current is non-zero, play() is never called for the new steps. Meanwhile the old playback's timer chain keeps running and reads stepsRef.current — which useDemoPlayback reassigns to the NEW steps during render (useDemoPlayback.ts line 49) — so the old chain continues at its old index into the new steps array: the first N imported people are silently skipped (left unassigned, because handleImport just reset everyone to area null) and progress/total are inconsistent. Traced scenario: start animated import of 20 people, at step 8 open the import dialog and import a second animated file — the new playback proceeds from index 9 of the new list and people 1-9 stay unassigned with no way to notice except manually.
suggestedFix: Replace the render-phase block with a useEffect keyed on the steps array identity: `useEffect(() => { if (playbackSteps.length > 0) playback.play(); }, [playbackSteps]);` — play() already resets/clears any running chain.

title: When Supabase is unconfigured and demo mode is off, the login form is a silent dead end — login() no-ops without setting any error
detail: If NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL/ANON_KEY are missing and NEXT_PUBLIC_DEMO_MODE is not exactly "true" (e.g. forgot the env var, or set it to "1"), then isDemoMode is false, user stays null, isLoading initializes to false, and AuthGuard renders the LoginPrompt. The misconfiguration is completely invisible to the operator standing at the wall display.

title: Case-sensitive .csv check routes uppercase-extension CSVs through Latin-1 path, corrupting all Chinese text
detail: isCSV() matches the extension case-sensitively, but ImportDialog.tsx (line 88) accepts extensions case-insensitively: `const ext = file.name.slice(file.name.lastIndexOf(".")).toLowerCase()`. title: Hand-rolled Database type fails supabase-js generic resolution, forcing `as any` on every query and disabling the type checking that would have caught the UUID bugs
detail: database.types.ts is hand-written rather than generated by `supabase gen types`, and its shape does not resolve against supabase-js v2's GenericSchema constraint — acknowledged in the code itself: every single query in useBoard.ts, audit-client.ts and useAuditLog.ts is wrapped in `(supabase.from(...) as any)` with the comment 'Supabase v2.106 GenericSchema resolution bug'. With `as any`, none of the Insert/Row types are enforced, which is precisely why passing area names into from_area_id/area_id (UUID columns) and 'demo-1' into person_id compiled without error. The type definitions exist but protect nothing. This is schema-vs-types drift in effect: the compile-time contract is disconnected from every runtime query.
